title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models: A Survey
authors: Yunfan Gao, Yun Xiong, Xinyu Gao, Kangxiang Jia, Jinliu Pan, Yuxi Bi, Yi Dai, Jiawei Sun, Wang, Meng, Wang, Haofen

screening.reason: Foundational survey covering RAG paradigms (Naive, Advanced, Modular), tripartite foundation (retrieval, generation, augmentation), and evaluation frameworks. Essential for establishing the taxonomy of technical routes.

title: Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy
authors: Zhihong Shao, Yeyun Gong, Yelong Shen, Minlie Huang, Nan Duan, Weizhu Chen

screening.reason: Presents Iter-RetGen, a specific technical route for iterative retrieval-generation synergy, addressing the 'coupling' aspect of the research question with empirical evidence on multi-hop QA and reasoning.

title: DRAGIN: Dynamic Retrieval Augmented Generation based on the Real-time Information Needs of Large Language Models
authors: Weihang Su, Yichen Tang, Qingyao Ai, Zhijing Wu, Yiqun Liu

screening.reason: Introduces DRAGIN, a dynamic RAG framework that decides when and what to retrieve based on LLM information needs. Directly addresses the 'training/decision mechanism' and 'coupling' aspects.

title: Benchmarking Large Language Models in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Jiawei Chen, Hongyu Lin, Xianpei Han, Le Sun

screening.reason: Establishes RGB benchmark to evaluate fundamental RAG abilities (noise robustness, negative rejection, information integration, counterfactual robustness). Critical for the 'evaluation framework' and 'reliability' sub-themes.

title: Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine
authors: Guangzhi Xiong, Qiao Jin, Zhiyong Lu, Aidong Zhang

screening.reason: Proposes MIRAGE benchmark for medical RAG, evaluating over 1.8 trillion tokens across 41 combinations of corpora, retrievers, and LLMs. Provides evidence on the scaling properties and optimal settings for RAG.

title: A Survey on Retrieval-Augmented Text Generation for Large Language Models

screening.reason: A survey organizing RAG into pre-retrieval, retrieval, post-retrieval, and generation categories. Offers a structured perspective on the mechanics and progression of RAG techniques.

title: RULE: Reliable Multimodal RAG for Factuality in Medical Vision Language Models
authors: Peng Xia, Kangyu Zhu, Haoran Li, Hongtu Zhu, Yun Li, Gang Li, Linjun Zhang, Huaxiu Yao

screening.reason: Conducts a comprehensive study comparing RAG with Long-Context LLMs, proposing SELF-ROUTE to balance performance and cost. Directly addresses the 'computational cost' and 'efficiency' aspects.

title: Corrective Retrieval Augmented Generation
authors: Shi-Qi Yan, Jia-Chen Gu, Yun Zhu, Zhen-Hua Ling

screening.reason: Proposes Corrective RAG (CRAG) to improve robustness by evaluating retrieved documents and performing web searches. Addresses the 'reliability' and 'factuality' challenges in RAG.

title: Enhancing LLM Factual Accuracy with RAG to Counter Hallucinations: A Case Study on Domain-Specific Queries in Private Knowledge-Bases
authors: Jiarui Li, Ye Yuan, Zehua Zhang

screening.reason: Case study on using RAG to counter hallucinations in domain-specific queries. Demonstrates the effectiveness of RAG in improving factual accuracy compared to fine-tuning alone.

title: Improving Retrieval Augmented Language Model with Self-Reasoning
authors: Yuan Xia, Jingbo Zhou, Zhenhui Shi, Jun Chen, Haifeng Huang

screening.reason: Proposes a self-reasoning framework for RALM to improve reliability and traceability. Addresses the 'reliability' and 'traceability' aspects of the research question.

title: Use of Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Model for COVID-19 Fact-Checking: Development and Usability Study
authors: Hai Li, Jingyi Huang, Mengmeng Ji, Yuyi Yang, Ruopeng An

screening.reason: Develops RAG-enhanced models for COVID-19 fact-checking, comparing Naive RAG, LOTR-RAG, CRAG, and SRAG. Provides empirical evidence on reducing hallucinations in fact-checking tasks.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for AI-Generated Content: A Survey
authors: Penghao Zhao, Hailin Zhang, Qinhan Yu, Zhengren Wang, Yunteng Geng, Fangcheng Fu, L. Yang, Wentao Zhang, Jiang, Jie, Cui, Bin

screening.reason: Survey on RAG for AI-Generated Content, classifying RAG foundations and summarizing enhancements. Covers the 'training' and 'augmentation' aspects in the context of AIGC.
